title: Projective morphisms with finite fibres are finite
statement: Let $f:D\to T$ be a projective morphism [def-pc-projective-morphism] with Noetherian target (that is, $T$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact). If every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] has only finitely many points, then $f$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

proof.text: Projectivity supplies properness by [lem-pc-projective-proper], as implemented by IsHProjective.isProper. Apply the proper-with-finite-fibres criterion [thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres]; it remains to prove each set-theoretic fibre finite.

Fix t and let g: Spec(overline(kappa(t))) -> T be the geometric point of [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. The residue-field morphism is constant with value t (Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply), and Spec(overline(kappa(t))) is nonempty since it is the spectrum of a field. Hence range(g) = {t}. Apply the chosen-pullback case of [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image], namely Scheme.Pullback.range_fst, to obtain range(pullback.fst f g) = f^{-1}({t}). Its source is the finite geometric fibre by hypothesis, so this range is a finite set (Set.finite_range). This also covers an empty geometric fibre. Together with properness, the criterion in step 1 proves finiteness.
